title: Opaque tuning layer and stable pin manifest for MHA/GQA/MoE
creator: Asha Menon
description: Goal: Provide a stable, auditable mechanism to publish per-model kernel/compile tuning decisions for MHA, GQA, and MoE models that decouples the compiler heuristics from runtime routing. Deliverables: 1) Opaque Tuning Layer (OTL): a thin adapter between the model-onboarder and the compiler that consumes signed pin manifests and exposes a deterministic API for kernel selection; 2) Pin Manifest v2 schema and signer workflow to publish versioned, rollback-capable tuning bundles; 3) CI verification, telemetry gates, and rollout playbook (canary -> ramp -> force-rollback). Rationale: Existing compile pins are tightly coupled to internal compiler state and require invasive rollbacks when regressions occur. The OTL makes tuning decisions explicit, signed, and verifiable, enabling safer rollouts and faster recoveries for production LLM workloads, especially sharded MoE and grouped-attention GQA where kernel choices materially affect memory and latency. Success metrics: - No customer-facing regressions during a pin rollout (target 0 incidents) - Average p95 token latency regression <= 3% across pinned workloads - Pin publish -> canary complete in < 2 hours (end-to-end) Key constraints and trade-offs: - Pins must remain small (<= 128KB) to fit in cache metadata and KMS signing limits; this favors compact hints over full IR dumps. - OTL will not replace compiler autotuning; it is an override/advice layer with safety checks and telemetry gating. - For MoE, we need per-shard heuristics vs global heuristics; initial implementation will include shard-affinity references but fall back to global variants for compatibility. Major design decisions: - Pin Manifest v2 fields: manifest_id, model_fingerprint, compatible_model_versions (list), kernel_alternatives (list of {op, variant_id, priority, expected_latency_ms, memory_delta_bytes}), quant_profile_ref, fallback_manifest_id, signed_metadata (signature metadata). - All manifests MUST include a compatibility checksum computed from model graph fingerprint to avoid accidental cross-model pins. - Publish flow: dev -> sign with ksm-key -> canary tag -> auto-canary job deploys to 1% of traffic -> telemetry check (p95, mem, error-rate) -> ramp. - Rollback token: manifest includes a single-token rollback id that runtime honors for instantaneous reversion without needing compiler re-publish. Testing plan: - Unit tests for manifest parsing and validation in onboarding service. - Deterministic selection simulator (python harness) to run candidate manifests against representative trace corpus (MHA/GQA/MoE traces) and produce perf delta report. - End-to-end canary on dedicated capacity pool with synthetic workload and subset of customer traces. Observability: - New telemetry keys: pin.manifest_id, pin.variant_chosen, pin.selection_reason, pin_latency_delta_ms, pin_memory_delta_bytes. - Dashboards: per-model pin adoption, p95 delta, memory delta, error-rate, and canary status. Security and audit: - Manifests are signed with KMS-managed signing key. Publish actions recorded in audit log with author, timestamp, manifest_id, and target rollout. - Optional HSM signing for enterprise private deployments. Backwards compatibility and migration: - Runtime will accept legacy pins (compat adapter) and treat them as low-priority manifests. - A migration job will scan existing pins and emit v2 manifest suggestions where possible. Open questions: - Should manifest include per-sequence-length performance buckets (short/medium/long) or a single expected_latency_ms? We chose single for v2 to keep size small, but will consider v3 with buckets. - How to represent MoE expert placement hints safely across shard topologies? Current plan: include an expert_affinity token and allow runtime to map it to local shard indices. See design doc for details.
comments: 2026-02-15 — Kickoff meeting notes: agreed on OTL API shape and high-level rollout flow. Action: Marco to prototype manifest validator.

2026-02-23 — PoC validator completed. Found ambiguity in fallback_manifest_id semantics; resolved to require explicit boolean allow_fallback flag in validation layer. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboarder/pull/402

2026-03-01 — Integration test harness run against MHA traces (squad of 8 traces). Observed median latency improvement 6% with mha_opt_v7; one trace showed 12% p95 regression because of long tail — added telemetry gate and reduced canary traffic for similar manifests.

notes_for_support: If a customer reports a latency regression after a pinned manifest rollout, support should: 1) collect manifest_id from runtime logs (pin.manifest_id), 2) check canary telemetry (link above) and rollout window, 3) if still within canary, flip rollout to fallback_manifest_id via rollback token and create incident. Include manifest_id and variant_chosen in incident ticket.
